analysis:
Examined the add-on hold surface: DaemonState.addonHold field (DaemonStateFile.swift:105-107, 354-356), LifecycleMailbox add-on request/status/claim (LifecycleMailbox.swift:28-55), ProviderDrain.Owner.addonHold with refusingForServiceChange and resumeAddonHold (ProviderDrain.swift:6-34), and the new `darkbloom addon` CLI (AddonCommand.swift).

The mailbox keeps the existing controls. The directory must be owned by the current uid with mode 0700 (lstat). Files are opened with O_NOFOLLOW, and the file must be owned by the current uid, regular, mode 0600 and at most 8 KB. Writes are temp file plus rename, and claims are an atomic rename. The `claim` refactor preserves the previous switch-claim behavior byte for byte. Requests are bound to ProcessIdentity (pid and start time), and the CLI checks identity.isCurrent() and state freshness before sending. The status response is matched by request ID. The trust boundary is the same-uid local user, which is already inside the TB-003 operator model. That user can already stop or drain the provider, so a same-uid hold is a local availability lever and not a privilege escalation.

ProviderDrain: begin() leaves .lifecycle (stop) as the strongest owner and lets only a stop preempt a hold. An update or reconnect resuming cannot reopen a hold. Setting refusingForServiceChange to false for an addon hold means startup and App Attest recovery treat the provider as serving. This depends on call sites outside the supplied diff: the ProviderLoop code that uses the new property and the add-on socket handler. I could not check that the hold still closes admission everywhere, or that model unload and attestation or connection invalidation stay authoritative. The T-053/T-057 interaction (hold versus grant application, revocation and connection change) is unverified.

Unverified contracts: AddonHoldControlRequest validation (leaseSecondsRange, isValid and target binding) and AddonHoldSnapshot/Status content are defined outside this batch. The `--force` release while the machine lock is held is only an operator debug override. The add-on local socket authentication is also outside the batch. The DaemonState file is not owner-restricted, and addonHold exposes only hold metadata (addon name, state and lease times). I see no confidentiality regression against A-001. No findings, but the loop and socket integration should be checked.
